instruction: Write API reference documentation for `POST /v1/users` that creates a user with email and name.
output:
## Create a user

`POST /v1/users`

Creates a new user account. Email addresses are unique per organization.

### Request body
| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------------|
| `email` | string | yes | Unique email address |
| `name` | string | yes | Display name, 1-100 chars |
| `role` | string | no | One of `member`, `admin` (default `member`) |

### Example
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.acme.io/v1/users \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"email":"ada@example.com","name":"Ada"}'
```

### Response `201 Created`
```json
{ "id": "usr_8f2", "email": "ada@example.com", "name": "Ada", "role": "member" }
```

### Errors
| Status | Code | Meaning |
|--------|------|---------|
| 400 | `invalid_field` | Missing or malformed field |
| 409 | `email_taken` | Email already exists |

## Retrieve a user

`GET /v1/users/{id}`

Returns a single user by ID.

### Path parameters
| Name | Type | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `id` | string | User ID (`usr_*`) |

### Example
```bash
curl https://api.acme.io/v1/users/usr_8f2 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```

### Response `200 OK`
```json
{ "id": "usr_8f2", "email": "ada@example.com", "name": "Ada", "role": "member", "created_at": "2025-03-01T10:00:00Z" }
```

### Errors
- `404 not_found` — no user with that ID, or it belongs to another organization.

instruction: Write API reference documentation for `GET /v1/users` including pagination.
output:
## List users

`GET /v1/users`

Returns users ordered by `created_at` descending, newest first.

### Query parameters
| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `limit` | integer | 20 | Page size, 1-100 |
| `cursor` | string | — | Opaque cursor from the previous page |
| `role` | string | — | Filter by role |

### Example
```bash
curl "https://api.acme.io/v1/users?limit=2&role=admin" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```

### Response `200 OK`
```json
{
  "data": [ { "id": "usr_8f2", "name": "Ada" } ],
  "next_cursor": "eyJvIjoyMH0"
}
```

Pass `next_cursor` back as `cursor` to fetch the next page. A `null` cursor means the end.

## Update a user

`PATCH /v1/users/{id}`

Partially updates a user. Only the fields present in the body are changed.

### Request body
Any subset of:
| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `name` | string | New display name |
| `role` | string | `member` or `admin` |
| `active` | boolean | Enable or disable the account |

### Example
```bash
curl -X PATCH https://api.acme.io/v1/users/usr_8f2 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"role":"admin"}'
```

### Response `200 OK`
Returns the full, updated user object.

### Notes
Setting `active` to `false` invalidates all of the user's sessions immediately.

## Delete a user

`DELETE /v1/users/{id}`

Soft-deletes a user. The record is retained for 30 days and can be restored by support.

### Example
```bash
curl -X DELETE https://api.acme.io/v1/users/usr_8f2 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```

### Response `204 No Content`
No body is returned.

### Idempotency
Calling delete on an already-deleted user returns `204` as well, so retries are safe.

### Errors
| Status | Code | Meaning |
|--------|------|---------|
| 403 | `last_admin` | Cannot delete the final admin |

## Log in

`POST /v1/auth/login`

Exchanges credentials for an access token and a refresh token.

### Request body
| Field | Type | Required |
|-------|------|----------|
| `email` | string | yes |
| `password` | string | yes |

### Example
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.acme.io/v1/auth/login \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"email":"ada@example.com","password":"s3cret"}'
```

### Response `200 OK`
```json
{
  "access_token": "eyJhbGci...",
  "refresh_token": "rt_9c1",
  "expires_in": 3600,
  "token_type": "Bearer"
}
```

### Errors
- `401 invalid_credentials` — email or password is wrong. The message is intentionally identical for unknown emails.

## Refresh an access token

`POST /v1/auth/refresh`

Issues a new access token using a refresh token. Refresh tokens are single-use and rotate on every call.

### Request body
| Field | Type | Required |
|-------|------|----------|
| `refresh_token` | string | yes |

### Example
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.acme.io/v1/auth/refresh \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"refresh_token":"rt_9c1"}'
```

### Response `200 OK`
```json
{ "access_token": "eyJhbGci...", "refresh_token": "rt_4x8", "expires_in": 3600 }
```

### Errors
- `401 token_reused` — the presented token was already rotated. All tokens for the user are revoked as a precaution.

## Create an order

`POST /v1/orders`

Places an order for one or more line items. Totals are computed server-side.

### Request body
| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------------|
| `items` | array | yes | At least one line item |
| `items[].sku` | string | yes | Product SKU |
| `items[].qty` | integer | yes | Quantity, >= 1 |
| `currency` | string | yes | ISO-4217 code |

### Example
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.acme.io/v1/orders \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"currency":"usd","items":[{"sku":"tee_blk_m","qty":2}]}'
```

### Response `201 Created`
```json
{ "id": "ord_71a", "status": "pending", "total": 5000, "currency": "usd" }
```

Amounts are integers in the smallest currency unit (cents).

## Get order status

`GET /v1/orders/{id}/status`

Returns the current lifecycle state of an order.

### Path parameters
| Name | Type | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `id` | string | Order ID (`ord_*`) |

### Response `200 OK`
```json
{ "id": "ord_71a", "status": "shipped", "updated_at": "2025-03-04T09:12:00Z" }
```

### Status values
| Status | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| `pending` | Accepted, not yet paid |
| `paid` | Payment captured |
| `shipped` | Handed to carrier |
| `cancelled` | Cancelled before shipping |

The endpoint is safe to poll; responses are served from a read replica.

## Create a webhook

`POST /v1/webhooks`

Registers an HTTPS endpoint to receive event deliveries.

### Request body
| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------------|
| `url` | string | yes | HTTPS URL to call |
| `events` | array | yes | Event types, e.g. `order.paid` |
| `secret` | string | no | Used to sign deliveries |

### Example
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.acme.io/v1/webhooks \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"url":"https://example.com/hook","events":["order.paid"]}'
```

### Delivery format
Each request includes `X-Acme-Signature`, an HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body using your `secret`.

### Retries
Failed deliveries retry with exponential backoff for up to 24 hours.

instruction: Write GraphQL API reference documentation for a `products` query with filtering.
output:
## Query: `products`

Returns a paginated connection of products.

### Signature
```graphql
products(first: Int = 20, after: String, filter: ProductFilter): ProductConnection!
```

### Arguments
| Name | Type | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `first` | Int | Page size, 1-100 |
| `after` | String | Cursor from `pageInfo.endCursor` |
| `filter` | ProductFilter | Optional filters |

### `ProductFilter`
```graphql
input ProductFilter { title: String, inStock: Boolean, minPrice: Int }
```

### Example
```graphql
query {
  products(first: 2, filter: { inStock: true }) {
    edges { cursor node { id title price } }
    pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor }
  }
}
```

Use `edges.node` for results and `pageInfo` for pagination.

instruction: Write GraphQL API reference documentation for a `createReview` mutation.
output:
## Mutation: `createReview`

Adds a review to a product for the authenticated user.

### Signature
```graphql
createReview(input: CreateReviewInput!): CreateReviewPayload!
```

### Input
```graphql
input CreateReviewInput { productId: ID!, rating: Int!, body: String }
```

`rating` must be between 1 and 5.

### Example
```graphql
mutation {
  createReview(input: { productId: "prod_1", rating: 4, body: "Great fit" }) {
    review { id rating }
    errors { field message }
  }
}
```

### Payload
| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `review` | Review | Null when `errors` is non-empty |
| `errors` | [UserError!]! | Validation failures |

Mutations return errors in the payload rather than throwing, so clients can render them inline.

instruction: Write API reference documentation for a gRPC method `GetInventory`.
output:
## GetInventory

`rpc GetInventory(GetInventoryRequest) returns (GetInventoryResponse)`

Returns available stock for a set of SKUs.

### Request
```proto
message GetInventoryRequest {
  repeated string skus = 1;  // max 100
  string warehouse_id = 2;   // optional
}
```

### Response
```proto
message GetInventoryResponse {
  message Item { string sku = 1; int32 available = 2; }
  repeated Item items = 1;
}
```

### Errors
| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| `INVALID_ARGUMENT` | More than 100 SKUs or empty list |
| `UNAVAILABLE` | Warehouse temporarily unreachable |

Unknown SKUs are omitted from `items` rather than causing an error.

## Create a charge

`POST /v1/payments/charge`

Charges a stored payment method and returns the resulting payment intent.

### Request body
| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------------|
| `amount` | integer | yes | Smallest currency unit |
| `currency` | string | yes | ISO-4217 code |
| `method_id` | string | yes | Stored payment method |
| `idempotency_key` | string | yes | Unique per logical charge |

### Example
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.acme.io/v1/payments/charge \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"amount":5000,"currency":"usd","method_id":"pm_2"}'
```

### Response `201 Created`
```json
{ "id": "pi_88", "status": "succeeded", "amount": 5000 }
```

Always send a unique `Idempotency-Key` so that network retries do not double-charge.

instruction: Write API reference documentation for `GET /v1/search` with query parameters.
output:
## Search

`GET /v1/search`

Full-text search across products and articles.

### Query parameters
| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `q` | string | — | Query string, required |
| `type` | string | `all` | `product`, `article`, or `all` |
| `limit` | integer | 10 | Results per page, 1-50 |

### Example
```bash
curl "https://api.acme.io/v1/search?q=wool+socks&type=product" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```

### Response `200 OK`
```json
{
  "query": "wool socks",
  "results": [ { "type": "product", "id": "sku_9", "score": 3.2 } ]
}
```

### Ranking
Results are ranked by BM25; `score` is the raw relevance score and is not comparable across queries.

instruction: Write API reference documentation for `POST /v1/files` multipart upload.
output:
## Upload a file

`POST /v1/files`

Uploads a file using `multipart/form-data`.

### Form fields
| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------------|
| `file` | file | yes | Max 25 MB |
| `purpose` | string | yes | e.g. `avatar`, `attachment` |

### Example
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.acme.io/v1/files \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -F "purpose=avatar" \
  -F "file=@photo.png"
```

### Response `201 Created`
```json
{ "id": "file_3k", "bytes": 20480, "content_type": "image/png" }
```

### Errors
| Status | Code | Meaning |
|--------|------|---------|
| 413 | `too_large` | Exceeds the 25 MB limit |
| 415 | `unsupported_type` | Content type not allowed for the purpose |

## Daily report

`GET /v1/reports/daily`

Returns aggregated metrics for a single day.

### Query parameters
| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `date` | string | yes | `YYYY-MM-DD` (UTC) |
| `metrics` | string | no | Comma-separated list; defaults to all |

### Example
```bash
curl "https://api.acme.io/v1/reports/daily?date=2025-03-01&metrics=orders,revenue" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```

### Response `200 OK`
```json
{
  "date": "2025-03-01",
  "metrics": { "orders": 412, "revenue": 1834500 }
}
```

Reports are computed once at 02:00 UTC for the previous day. Requesting today's date returns `404 not_ready`.

## Send a notification

`POST /v1/notifications/send`

Sends a notification over one or more channels.

### Request body
| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------------|
| `user_id` | string | yes | Recipient |
| `channels` | array | yes | Subset of `email`, `sms`, `push` |
| `template` | string | yes | Template key |
| `data` | object | no | Template variables |

### Example
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.acme.io/v1/notifications/send \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"user_id":"usr_8f2","channels":["email"],"template":"order_shipped","data":{"order":"ord_71a"}}'
```

### Response `202 Accepted`
```json
{ "id": "ntf_5", "status": "queued" }
```

Delivery is asynchronous. If a channel is unavailable, the others still proceed.

instruction: Write API reference documentation for a WebSocket endpoint `wss://api.acme.io/ws/events`.
output:
## Events WebSocket

`wss://api.acme.io/ws/events`

Streams account events in real time.

### Connecting
```js
const ws = new WebSocket('wss://api.acme.io/ws/events');
ws.onopen = () => ws.send(JSON.stringify({ type: 'auth', token: TOKEN }));
ws.onmessage = (e) => console.log(JSON.parse(e.data));
```
The first frame must be an `auth` message; the server closes the socket otherwise.

### Server messages
| `type` | Fields | Description |
|--------|--------|-------------|
| `event` | `name`, `payload` | A domain event |
| `pong` | — | Reply to a client `ping` |
| `error` | `code`, `message` | Non-fatal problem |

### Keep-alive
Send `{"type":"ping"}` at least every 30 seconds or the server disconnects you.

instruction: Write API reference documentation for health and metrics endpoints.
output:
## Health and metrics

Two operational endpoints are exposed on a separate port.

### `GET /healthz`
Returns `200` when the service can serve traffic, `503` otherwise.
```json
{ "status": "ok", "checks": { "db": "ok", "cache": "ok" } }
```
Readiness (`/readyz`) additionally verifies downstream dependencies; use it for load-balancer gating.

### `GET /metrics`
Prometheus text format. Key series:
| Metric | Type | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| `http_requests_total` | counter | Requests by `route` and `status` |
| `http_request_duration_seconds` | histogram | Latency buckets |
| `build_info` | gauge | Always `1`, labeled with the release version |

These endpoints require no authentication but are bound to the internal network only.
